measured_at: admission probes (crucible.rapid.admission.admit) on seeds 0-2 and 10-12, single-CPU, wave 3b; not official evidence (D-24)

baseline_integrated_tree.note: pe_stream_processor fell out after the D-20 line-metering merge (its reference program was priced out of its margin)

M.1.notes: Robustly admitted training families (all eleven checks on seeds 0-2 and 10-12): 18 on the integrated tree at the start of wave 3, 22 after the claim and identification repairs (snapshot of df2f24b). 60 are required. The binding check is no_dominant_strategy under H-D1: in most primitive-graph lever families a hindsight-tuned constant reaches >= 0.9 of the evaluator's upper reference, i.e. the worlds are static-tuning worlds; they need redesign, not a weaker criterion.

M.2.notes: 8 robustly admitted evaluation families (partition v5-eval-1) of 28 registered; 20 required. The 18 4.0 val/test families are untouched and not counted.

M.3.notes: All ten categories have a robustly admitted family; 8.1 only through sci_dose_response (8.1.3), 8.8 only through the evaluation family strat_learning_rival.

M.4.notes: Nine v5 engines with robustly admitted families plus the three preserved 4.0 engines; no v5 engine module imports another.

M.5.notes: Every family has a measured, purely categorical nine-component fingerprint; engines now declare observation channels (aggregated routing separates net_hidden_bottleneck_swap from net_topology_shift).

M.6.notes: Robustly admitted families offer levers, discrete, allocate, coordinate, message, query, experiment, program and sequence.

M.7.notes: Feasibility (consistency, conservation, achievable on every seed of both sets) holds for 86-87 of 88 registered families with 0 admitted without it; the criterion counts 80 validated families - see the gate run for the exact count.

M.8.notes: 88 of 88 families' controlled-intervention claims pass on seeds 0-2 and 10-12 (0 failures; 14 claims repaired in wave 3, the known-failure xfail list is empty).

M.n1.notes: Renamed, parameter and difficulty-axis variants of every family; fingerprint version rapid-fp/2.

SP-0.9.notes: 18 4.0 val/test families fingerprinted from their engines; 60 v5 training families checked; 0 match by distance or mechanism recreation (recreation now also against 4.0 validation families, H-D2).

SP-7.0.notes: 5 goal kinds generated from the public face and validated feasible on >= 3 engines each; 0 families whose default objective is not scored by its type's generic rule; 88/88 objective-free; generator statically independent of worlds. Limitation: builders still declare a default objective.

SP-7.2.notes: compose varies 11 dimensions, each verified by doing the same thing in both worlds on seeds 0-2 (with a same-recipe negative control); 6 of 6 look-alike market pairs separated by the price-response protocol.

SP-7.4.notes: Eleven checks, each rejecting a broken control world.

SP-7.5.notes: Pair protocols added for the three pairs the response signature could not separate (dose response vs hypotheses, inventory vs perishable, routing vs topology shift).

SP-8.0.notes: 4 of the 60 named items have no family (8.5.1, 8.5.4, 8.6.5, 8.7.5); most registered items have no robustly admitted family.

SP-8.0b.notes: Six category requirements measured on robustly admitted families. Expected unmet: 8.2 (lab_drift_blanks scores a held-out dose inside the settable range) and 8.8 (no robustly admitted 8.8 training family, so no training opponent population).

SP-8.12.notes: Nine difficulty axes; batch path aggregate-routing fix.

SP-8.12b.notes: 45 of 45 batchable families equal to single worlds; a learner through RapidVecEnv runs 74,500 world-steps per CPU-s (target 20,000, H-D3) and 17x the single-world path (target 10x).

limitations: Gate M counts are far below 60 training / 20 evaluation families under the H-D1 dominance criterion; most primitive-graph lever families (hc_*, cx_*, cxc_*, cxs_*, mk_*, ch_demand_shift/tech_transition/constraint_tightens/drifting_ideal) are static-tuning worlds and need redesign so that their optimum is not a constant.

Program-execution families pay for compute by parent-measured CPU time (D-20); their admission values depend on machine load (pe_stream_processor's reference earned 857 in one run and 703 in another, same code and seed).
Four named Part 8 items have no family: 8.5.1 hidden opportunities with costly investigation, 8.5.4 uncertain investment, 8.6.5 irreversible commitments, 8.7.5 distributed resource coordination.
A redesign of hc_conditional as a hidden switching gate (requires repeated intervention) was tried in wave 3 and reverted: its tracker reference did not beat hindsight threshold rules robustly.

Several program and planning references still read their own configuration for sandbox plumbing; wave 3 removed hidden reads only from the references audited as public (lever roles, prizes, damages, dig cost, payoff scale).
net_topology_shift's claim fails on seeds 3, 5 and 9 (outside the admission seed sets).
integration_notes: program_exec compute cost consumes the parent-measured CPU of workstream O's sandbox metering; for reproducible Tier 1 admission a deterministic parent-side measure (calls x price, or quantised CPU recorded as an external event and replayed in admission) is recommended. Not changed here (O owns metering).
crucible.rapid.vec.RapidVecEnv is a learner-facing batched interface (observation_only, reward 0.0); workstream L may expose it through crucible.experience.
D-9 recreation now includes 4.0 validation families; three families moved from v5-train to v5-eval-1 (ch_sign_reversal, ch_rule_change, ch_wandering_taste).
